pages.passage: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) are analogs of EPO and widely used in end-stage renal disease–related anemia and patients with MDS with moderate to severe anemia. Data on application of ESAs in other causes of anemia including UAE are limited.

directoryStems.mcq-d989e8f41faf9358b2743e5f: After a dose of oral iron, which response helps explain why alternate-day administration can improve fractional absorption?
directoryStems.mcq-4caa65474b9733a526dfd9b6: A 78-year-old man with chronic kidney disease and stable normocytic anemia is being evaluated. Nutritional deficiencies have not yet been assessed. What should be done before attributing the anemia to kidney disease and choosing treatment?
directoryStems.mcq-491e8548e27bbf805f604686: An 82-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis has confirmed iron-deficiency anemia. She is stable, has no ischemic symptoms, and can take oral medication. Which initial replacement strategy is generally preferred in Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-e8482e204c5ed512bec605e9: A 78-year-old woman with normocytic anemia and fatigue has undergone iron studies, vitamin B12 and folate testing, kidney and thyroid testing, assessment for inflammation, and hematologic evaluation. No nutritional deficiency, inflammatory process, kidney disease, or hematologic disease explaining the anemia has been identified. Which designation applies at this stage?
directoryStems.mcq-38291965ee27947e59371896: An 82-year-old frail man with heart failure and chronic kidney disease has iron-deficiency anemia (hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL, ferritin 15 ng/mL). He lives in assisted living and has difficulty adhering to medications. His daughter is concerned about frequent clinic visits. Which oral iron schedule does Hazzard generally prefer for initial replacement?
directoryStems.mcq-4bc455efd05c6f1c86df64a8: A 75-year-old woman with chronic anemia from myelodysplastic syndrome previously had no symptoms at a low baseline hemoglobin. Her hemoglobin is now 7.6 g/dL, with new chest pain and dyspnea on minimal exertion consistent with end-organ ischemia. Which transfusion approach matches Hazzard’s discussion on page 1480?
directoryStems.mcq-f0e487f2b65842ecf04ed41d: A 69-year-old man is found to have new anemia on routine testing. There are currently no findings suggesting a hematologic malignancy, and no etiologic work-up has been performed. Which group of tests belongs in the initial evaluation described by Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-71fc7746ea319783cc9fe74d: An 84-year-old frail woman with dementia and multiple comorbidities has chronic hemolytic anemia, a stable baseline hemoglobin of 6.0 g/dL, no anemia symptoms, and preserved usual daily activities at that level. Her family asks for transfusion to make her feel better. Which approach follows Hazzard’s example of asymptomatic chronic hemolytic anemia?
directoryStems.mcq-38a795de141595e2fc888769: An initial anemia work-up in an older adult identifies no nutritional deficiency or impaired renal function. Which observation does Hazzard describe in studies of unexplained anemia in older adults?
directoryStems.mcq-a792bb8ad54498d29487046c: A 71-year-old with iron-deficiency anemia has almost no hemoglobin response after six weeks of oral iron and cannot tolerate the gastrointestinal effects. Which replacement strategy does Hazzard identify in this situation?
directoryStems.mcq-91de2309a478f854812e5404: A 76-year-old woman with anemia and chronic kidney disease has unexplained weight loss. Before deciding whether to give an erythropoiesis-stimulating agent, what approach to evaluating the anemia is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-4e6ac123c2f829c3e574dbd1: A frail 85-year-old resident with chronic anemia finds frequent clinic visits difficult. Treatment has not yet been selected, and the team is defining its goal. Which principle accords with Hazzard's approach to anemia in older adults?
directoryStems.mcq-ef85d0464735b7a8d81f6c21: An older adult with iron-deficiency anemia is clinically stable, tolerates oral iron, and has no known problem with absorption. Which statement about iron replacement agrees with Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-2a937050d9430d7a30da21d6: A patient with iron-deficiency anemia is preparing for joint replacement. She cannot tolerate oral iron and still requires iron replacement. Which alternative is described in Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-cbfe7f3cff9bc361d44a5610: In its discussion of aging mechanisms, how does Hazzard describe inflammaging?
directoryStems.mcq-e9d568ecc9ed6a625e61c6d7: A 78-year-old man with postoperative iron-deficiency anemia stopped an adequate oral iron regimen because of substantial intolerance. He is stable and has no active bleeding. Which method of iron replacement is supported by Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-fe3ed1ff87e9893db1784b95: A 77-year-old woman has iron-deficiency anemia. Which follow-up finding supports changing to intravenous iron under the recommendations in Hazzard’s anemia chapter?
directoryStems.mcq-fcceaa876c9a7e7df4d7b244: A 78-year-old man with iron-deficiency anemia is suitable for oral iron replacement. He tolerates oral therapy and does not need urgent transfusion. Which initial strategy and rationale match Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-401b01ce02c31c9f05cba4ae: A patient with chronic hemolytic anemia is asymptomatic at a baseline hemoglobin of 6 g/dL. A target of 7 g/dL is being considered. What consequence does the example in Hazzard describe?
directoryStems.mcq-22496d720618843a4687f939: Initial testing has not identified the cause of anemia in an older woman. When is the term unexplained anemia of the elderly appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-9d67cdf76b53fd3cdab0fa74: An 81-year-old woman with previously unevaluated anemia presents for an initial assessment. There is no specific suspicion of a hematologic malignancy. Which group of tests belongs in the initial work-up described in Hazzard?
